title: `move-draw-fire`: Called Out (Bulwark rank I, `class:defender.draw_fire`)
notes:

- **Save as:** `art/icons/moves/draw-fire.png` (replaces the placeholder `draw-fire.svg`).
- **Shows:** Class move card and the fight bar. Called Out: the Bulwark names a foe, and the foe has no choice but to answer the call.
paint: Wick facing right with a tower shield raised on his left arm, his right arm flung out straight and pointing, his head thrown back and forward as he shouts: three short broken call lines leap from his head toward the edge of the frame, where the cut-off silhouette of a single foe (just a shoulder and the point of a helm) is turning to look at him. staging: The shield is one tall slab with one rounded cut, attached behind by ONE left forearm. Other arm extends to the right calling toward a turning cropped shoulder/helmet. Clearly visible one point and three short call strokes. Preserve only one Wick.
label: Called Out (Bulwark rank I, `class:defender.draw_fire`)
prompt:
Draw one icon in pure white flat ink (#FFFFFF) on a fully transparent background, in exactly the style of the attached reference icons: Wick, the small figure of the trait and perk icons with the ceramic pixel-screen head, capelet and lantern heart, in bold flat white shapes, a confident inked silhouette with a few interior cuts, the same line weight. No outline in another colour, no shading, no gradient, no texture, no glow, no colour and no grey. Wick is the only full figure; anyone else is a partial (a hand, a shoulder, a silhouette cut by the frame). One action, centred, with clear space around it, square, 1024 x 1024 PNG with transparency. It must read at 32 px in a row and at 44 px on a chip: silhouette first, two or three interior cuts at most. No text, no letters, no numbers, no border, no frame. Invented shapes only: nothing recognisable from real-world works, brands, insignia or religions. The icon shows:
Wick facing right with a tower shield raised on his left arm, his right arm flung out straight and pointing, his head thrown back and forward as he shouts: three short broken call lines leap from his head toward the edge of the frame, where the cut-off silhouette of a single foe (just a shoulder and the point of a helm) is turning to look at him. The shield is the bulk of the picture, a bold rounded slab with one interior cut. The meaning is making a foe pick you. At icon size it must read as a shielded figure pointing and calling. Avoid: a speech bubble, letters, an exclamation mark, a megaphone, a target or bullseye, a taunting face, a second full figure.
Wick always has the exact approved oversized rounded ceramic screen head, transparent face recess with white pixel expression, ear discs, offset shell fittings, short asymmetric capelet, lantern-heart inset, chunky mitten hands and cuffed boots. The silhouette of the head ends at the smooth ceramic shell. There is NO flame, tuft, plume, candle or object attached to or above his head. Resolve any stale flame wording through the angle or pixel expression. Omit default floating cup and reference arrows.
The shield is one tall slab with one rounded cut, attached behind by ONE left forearm. Other arm extends to the right calling toward a turning cropped shoulder/helmet. Clearly visible one point and three short call strokes. Preserve only one Wick. 
All dark voids are physically transparent alpha cutouts, never solid black or gray. Clear border, stable negative space at game size, pure white flat ink.
